cards.text: Meet Absalom, son of King David. Some time later, he gets himself a chariot with horses, and he adds a little extra. Me? I get around by HOPPING on a gold base.

cards.question: Besides a chariot and horses, what else does Absalom provide for himself?

answers.text: Fifty men to run ahead of him
A hundred archers to guard him

cards.text: Absalom gets up EARLY and stands beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone comes along with a grievance for the king to decide, Absalom calls out to him.

cards.question: When Absalom calls out to someone bringing a grievance to the king, he asks what city the person is from.

cards.text: Say the man answers that he's from one of the tribes of Israel. Then Absalom tells him what he thinks of his case.

cards.question: Absalom tells the man from one of the tribes of Israel that his claims are weak and he should drop them.
Absalom says the man's claims are good and right. So what does Absalom say the problem is?

answers.text: The king has no deputy to hear him
The king's judges have been bribed
The king is busy fighting a war

cards.text: Then Absalom adds a wish. If only someone would give him a certain job, he says, everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to him, and he would give him justice.

cards.question: Absalom says he wishes someone would appoint him ___ in the land.

cards.text: And it's not just talk. When people come close to bow down to him, Absalom has a move ready for that too.

cards.question: What does Absalom do when someone approaches to bow down to him?

answers.text: Takes hold of him and kisses him
Lets him bow and walks away
Has his runners push him back

cards.text: Absalom does this to ALL the Israelites who come to the king for justice. This man is shaking more hands than a greeter at the church door on Easter Sunday.

cards.question: In this way, Absalom stole the ___ of the men of Israel.

cards.text: After four years pass, Absalom asks the king to let him go to Hebron to fulfill a vow he made to the LORD. He says he promised to worship the LORD in Hebron if the LORD brought him back to Jerusalem.

cards.question: Absalom says he made his vow to worship the LORD in Hebron while he was living somewhere else. Where?
King David turns down Absalom's request and tells him to stay in Jerusalem.

cards.text: So Absalom gets up and goes to Hebron, and then he sends spies throughout the tribes of Israel with a message. SPIES, friend, on a worship trip!

cards.question: Absalom's spies carry a message across the tribes of Israel. When the people hear the sound of the horn, what are they supposed to say?

cards.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem go along with Absalom. They were invited as guests.

cards.question: The two hundred guests from Jerusalem know all about Absalom's plan.

cards.text: While Absalom is offering the sacrifices, he sends for Ahithophel the Gilonite to come from his hometown of Giloh. Friend, this is NOT some random name on the guest list.

cards.question: Ahithophel the Gilonite isn't just anybody. He's David's ___.
As Ahithophel is called in, what happens to Absalom's following?

cards.text: The conspiracy is gaining strength. And that's where we'll pause for now, friend, because this story is FAR from over.

findings.problem: This is a 'which thing' question: what else Absalom provides for himself. The wrong answers 'Twelve trumpeters to announce him' and 'A hundred archers to guard him' are invented. They aren't real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'In this way,' which points back to the story card before it. That card is no longer on screen, so the question never says what Absalom did.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'the people' are the ones who hear the horn and say the line. In 2 Samuel 15:10 the message is 'When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say,' and the text leaves open whether 'you' means the spies or the tribes. The card decides who is being spoken to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Ahithophel shows up here for the first time, but the card holds back who he is ('this is NOT some random name on the guest list') so card 9 can ask about it. The first time someone appears, Papa Dorin should say simply who they are, here 'David's counselor' (2 Samuel 15:12). Card 9 then needs a different question.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The humor is thin across the walkthrough. Card 1's gold-base line is a mild aside more than a real laugh. Most of stop 2 reads as plain retelling, with only the 'SPIES, friend, on a worship trip!' line and the guest-list line. Moments like Absalom's early-morning roadside routine and the 200 guests who had no idea could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
